summary: Yoshihiko Sakurai is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Ryukoku University until 2001. He served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University and as a researcher at Kyogaku Dendo Kenkyu Senta until 2003.
Yoshihiro Hayashi works in the fields of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has held appointments as a part-time lecturer at both Ritsumeikan University and Shitennoji University.
Yoshitoyo Ohara is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Kyoto National Museum from circa 1997 to 2016 and at Kyoto University around 2016.

A Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, Muroji earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg (~1983–1992) under Lambert Schmithausen, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan. He held posts at Kyoto University, Koyasan University (~1993–2006), and Shiga University of Medical Science (~2006).
Yoshiko Shimabukuro is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Kyoto Chuo Bukkyo Gakuen until 1936 and subsequently at Kyoto Women's University from 1936 to 1940.

Yoshinobu Kimoto is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He served as an associate professor at Yonezawa Women's Junior College from circa 1984 to 1993, and held a post at Koshien Junior College from circa 1993 to 2003.

Yoshinori Takeuchi was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1933 to 1936, and later served there as a professor from circa 1959 to 1976.

Yoshio Kawakatsu specialized in Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1945–1948) and under Paul Demiéville (~1956–1959), and he held a post at Kyoto University from circa 1950 to 1984.

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Imaeda studied at Otani University (~1965–1969) and the EPHE (~1970–1974) under Ariane Macdonald and Bernard Frank. From circa 1981 to 2012, he served as a researcher at the CNRS.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Tamura studied at the University of Tokyo (~1946–1949). He held posts at Komazawa University, Toyo University (~1957–1964), the University of Tokyo (~1964–1982), Rissho University (~1982–1989), and the University of Chicago as Numata Professor (1985).

A scholar of Sinology and philosophy, Togawa studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1950 to 1959. He held posts at Tokyo Gakugei University (~1960–1969), Ochanomizu University (~1969–1982), the University of Tokyo (~1982–1992), and Nishogakusha University (~1992–2007).

Yoshitaka Iriya specialized in Sinology and Buddhist studies, studying at Kyoto University (~1933–1936). He held posts at Nagoya University (~1956–1968), Kyoto University (~1968–1974 as professor), Kyoto Sangyo University (~1974–1981), and Hanazono University (~1981–1986).

Yoshitsugu Sawai is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Tenri, Tohoku, and Harvard universities, earning a PhD under John B. Carman. He held academic posts at Tenri University from circa 1985 and Harvard University (~1995–1996).
Yoshiyuki Kawazoe studied at Tohoku University from circa 1966 to 1975. He subsequently held an academic post at Tohoku University from circa 1975 to 2012.
Yosho Nomura was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University from circa 1936 to 1939. He later served as director at Rissho University in 1980.

Youru Wang is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Temple University (~1990–1999) and held posts at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and Rowan University (beginning circa 1999).

Yozo Taniyama is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1992–2002). He held posts at Sophia University, St. Thomas University, Shitennoji University, and Tohoku University's Department of Practical Religious Studies (~2012).
Yu Yan Pang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. Pang earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong, studying under supervisors Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, as well as teacher Eric Kvan.

Yu-Chen Tsui is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's at Columbia University under Chun-fang Yu and a PhD at UCLA (~2011–2018) under Natasha Heller. Tsui also studied under traditional teacher Sheng Yen.

A Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, Ng studied at CUHK (~1965–1974) under Zongsan Mou and earned a PhD at McMaster (~1985–1990). He held posts at Hong Kong Baptist University (1988) and National Central University (~1995).
